name: Crowd Supply (hardware launch platform, Mouser-backed)
why: Crowd Supply positions itself as the launch platform for engineers and developers shipping open/dev hardware, with fulfillment handled by parent Mouser Electronics. It already hosted a wearable ECG/HRV dev product: ProtoCentral's HeartyPatch (single-lead ECG patch with HRV analysis, funded 2017) and the HealthyPi v4 vital-signs dev kit.
ask: Submit a pre-campaign application for the Vybe DevKit and ask the team for feedback on readiness and timing.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK and a small DevKit for developers. Your audience of engineers looks like the right first home for that kit. Could we get your team's read on whether it fits Crowd Supply and what you'd want to see before a campaign?
entry_route: Public application at crowdsupply.com/apply; the Crowd Supply Guide explains when to submit. Non-exclusive: after backers receive orders the creator may sell anywhere.
opportunity: Launch the DevKit (not the consumer band) to a developer audience, with Mouser fulfillment and continued distributor sales after the campaign; HeartyPatch shows the category is accepted.
unknowns: Fees/revenue share not found in search results. Reported ~90% rejection rate (Linux Magazine, secondary). Whether a closed/licensed SDK (vs open source) is acceptable is unknown; the platform is pitched at open-source hardware. Minimum unit volumes not found.

name: Truemed merchant program (HSA/FSA checkout + marketplace)
why: Truemed lets merchants accept HSA/FSA funds via a clinician-issued Letter of Medical Necessity and lists partners in its marketplace. Garmin partnered with Truemed in October 2025 for smartwatches and trackers; Truemed also lists the Amazfit Helio Ring and AIVELA Ring Pro.
why_now: Truemed raised a $34M Series A in December 2025 (Pulse 2.0); Garmin partnership October 2025.
ask: Book a 15-minute call with Truemed sales to ask how eligibility works for a general-wellness band and what onboarding costs.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band with no required subscription, launching to consumers in May 2027. I saw Garmin and several ring brands on Truemed. Could we have a short call about how merchant onboarding works for a pre-launch wearable and what you'd need from us?
entry_route: 'Talk to our team' form at truemed.com/merchant-sign-up; Truemed states go-live in under 7 days and sales response under 24 hours.
opportunity: Add HSA/FSA payment at Vybe checkout at launch and get listed in Truemed's marketplace alongside Garmin and ring brands.
unknowns: Merchant fees not found. Whether a general-wellness device (no medical claims) qualifies for an LMN is per product and unknown. Incremental-revenue figures on the sign-up page are Truemed's own claims.

name: Flex for Wearable Devices (HSA/FSA payments)
why: Flex has a dedicated wearables industry page saying it helps classify devices as 'always eligible' or 'dual purpose' with a Letter of Medical Necessity, and works with Shopify, custom sites or no-code. RingConn's Gen 2 smart ring is live on Flex's brand pages.
ask: Ask Flex for a demo and an eligibility review of a general-wellness ECG/HRV band before choosing an HSA/FSA partner.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band, consumer launch May 2027, no required subscription. Your wearables page says you help brands sort out HSA/FSA eligibility. Could we set up a short demo and talk through how you'd classify a device like ours?
entry_route: Contact/demo via the wearables industry page on withflex.com; a WooCommerce plugin and Shopify integration are listed.
opportunity: HSA/FSA checkout for the consumer launch; compare against Truemed and Sika on fees and eligibility handling. RingConn is a direct wearable precedent.
unknowns: Pricing not published (a third-party profile describes a subscription model). Performance claims (AOV, conversion) are Flex's own and conflict between pages. Eligibility of Vybe's band is unknown.

name: Sika Health (HSA/FSA checkout + marketplace)
why: Sika Health runs HSA/FSA checkout for e-commerce brands and a shopping marketplace that launched in December 2023 with 18,000+ eligible SKUs from 30+ brands, including health-monitoring wearables; Hyperice and Therabody are partners. Its regulatory team works with brands to check products against IRS rules.
ask: Request a merchant intro call to compare Sika's eligibility review with Truemed and Flex.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band for a May 2027 consumer launch, no required subscription. I read that your regulatory team works with brands like Hyperice on HSA/FSA eligibility. Could we have a short call about how that review works for a new wearable?
entry_route: No public merchant form surfaced in search; reach via Sika's website/sales team.
opportunity: HSA/FSA checkout plus a listing in Sika's marketplace next to recovery-tech brands.
unknowns: No 2026 news found; partner counts are from 2023. Merchant sign-up URL and fees not found in results. Eligibility of Vybe's band unknown.

name: FSA Store / HSA Store (Health-E Commerce) brand partnerships
why: Health-E Commerce, parent of FSA Store and HSA Store, partnered with Oura in November 2023 to sell the Oura Ring Horizon with FSA/HSA funds, and still ran Oura in a 2026 promotion. Benefits administrators (MedBen, P&A, HSA Bank) route their members to these stores.
why_now: Health-E Commerce added a Talkspace partnership (Digital Commerce 360, 2026-04-28).
ask: Ask for an intro to Health-E Commerce's brand partnerships team to learn listing requirements for a wellness wearable.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band, consumer launch May 2027, no required subscription. I saw Oura's partnership with FSA Store and HSA Store. Could you point me to whoever handles new brand partners, so I can learn what a listing would require?
entry_route: No published vendor form found; brand partnerships appear to be negotiated. Start via the company's site or LinkedIn business development.
opportunity: Listing in a 100%-eligible store that benefits administrators push to their members; Oura is the wearable precedent.
unknowns: No public supplier/brand application found. Whether the stores accept items that need an LMN (vs always-eligible) for a general-wellness band is unknown. Terms unknown. Owned by H.I.G. Capital since June 2024.

name: Amazon Launchpad (US)
why: Amazon's US Launchpad page describes a no-cost, invite-only program for up-and-coming brands (listing optimization, promotion, discounts) for up to 36 months. Amazon's other-country pages say it mainly considers brands backed by its collaborators: crowdfunding platforms, VCs and accelerators.
ask: Ask any accelerator or crowdfunding partner Vybe joins whether it is an Amazon Launchpad collaborator that can nominate brands.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band for a May 2027 consumer launch. We're planning our Amazon presence and read that Launchpad works with brands backed by accelerators and crowdfunding partners. Does your program have a Launchpad referral path, and what would we need to qualify?
entry_route: Invite-only in the US; get nominated via a Launchpad collaborator (accelerator, VC or crowdfunding platform). Other countries have open forms.
opportunity: Launch-period visibility on Amazon via invitation, building on the existing Seller Central/Brand Registry row.
unknowns: US entry is invite-only; the nominating partner list is not public. Third-party guides conflict on fees (one says 5% of sales; the US page says no-cost) and sales caps. FBA requirement is third-party, unverified.

name: Gadget Flow product listing
why: Gadget Flow's submission page takes physical products or functional prototypes with a public order/availability page, works with Kickstarter, Indiegogo, Shopify and Amazon stores, and promotes listings via social, apps and newsletters. Free submission plus paid marketing plans.
ask: Submit a free listing about 30 days before the pre-order or DevKit page goes live.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band, with pre-orders planned ahead of a May 2027 consumer launch. We'd like to submit it to Gadget Flow when our order page is live. Is there anything about a pre-launch listing we should prepare beyond the photos and video your guide asks for?
entry_route: Free submission at thegadgetflow.com/submit; editorial review within 24 hours, preview within 48 hours (Gadget Flow's stated timeline).
opportunity: Low-cost discovery listing for pre-orders/crowdfunding traffic, timed to the launch page.
unknowns: Paid plan prices not found in results. Audience figures conflict (6M official vs 31M claimed elsewhere). Needs a public order page, so not usable until pre-orders open.

name: Huckberry brand submission
why: Huckberry's help center says it is always looking for high-quality gear with a unique story and takes pitches through a 'Brand Suggestions' form that goes to its buying team. Huckberry is also a first-time exhibitor at The Running Event 2026, a sign it is buying into run specialty.
ask: Submit Vybe through the Brand Suggestions form once launch photos and pricing exist.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We make a screenless overnight band that records ECG and HRV with no required subscription, launching May 2027. It's built for people who train hard and don't want another screen. We'd love Huckberry's buying team to consider it for a launch drop, and can send samples when ready.
entry_route: Brand Suggestions form linked from Huckberry's help article; goes directly to buyers.
opportunity: Curated e-commerce drop to an outdoor/active men's audience at launch.
unknowns: Buying terms, margins and whether Huckberry carries wearables are not shown. Support team cannot answer brand-submission questions (their wording). Form is single-route only.

name: Academy Sports + Outdoors new vendor (Sports + Recreation buyer form)
why: Academy's help center sends prospective vendors to its 'Becoming an Academy Vendor' page and vendor.academy.com, with separate new-vendor buyer contact forms by department (including sports + recreation) and a dropship pre-screening questionnaire. Its FAQ sets product-liability insurance and SPS Commerce EDI requirements.
ask: Fill in the dropship pre-screening questionnaire to learn whether a pre-launch wearable can start online-only.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band for athletes, launching May 2027 with no required subscription. We're mapping sporting-goods retail and would like to know whether Academy's dropship program could fit a new wearable brand, and what your sports and recreation buyers look for first.
entry_route: Department-specific new-vendor buyer contact forms plus a dropship pre-screening questionnaire, linked from academy.com help and vendor.academy.com.
opportunity: Sporting-goods retail (dropship first, then stores) across Academy's South/Midwest footprint.
unknowns: Whether Academy carries this wearable category is unknown. Minimum product-liability limit is stated as required but the amount is not in results. Store counts vary by source (290-301).

name: Meijer prospective vendor / supplier diversity events (via RangeMe)
why: Meijer, a Midwest retailer with stores in Ohio, routes new-product submissions through RangeMe and has run general merchandise supplier events for certified diverse and locally owned brands in six Midwest states, with short video applications. Suppliers not selected stay in RangeMe for future buyer review.
ask: Create a RangeMe profile that also flags Meijer, and watch for the next Meijer general merchandise supplier event.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band, launching May 2027, with no required subscription. As an Ohio brand we'd like to be considered when Meijer next reviews general merchandise or electronics suppliers. What's the best way to get on your buyers' radar ahead of launch?
entry_route: Meijer prospective vendor page -> RangeMe profile; periodic supplier events (past ones used rangeme.com/meijerdiversity).
opportunity: Midwest mass-retail shelf for an Ohio-made-brand story; diverse/local supplier events give a structured entry.
unknowns: No 2025-2026 event date found; the cited events are undated (likely 2020-2022). Whether Meijer electronics buys wearables from new brands is unknown. Certification needed for diversity events (Vybe's certifications are tracked elsewhere).

name: The Running Event 2026 (run specialty retail trade show)
why: TRE is North America's run specialty retail conference and trade show, December 1-3, 2026 in San Antonio (20th edition). 274 brands had booked by May 2026, with first-time exhibitors such as Fabletics and Huckberry; it is the gathering point for independent running-store buyers.
why_now: Show runs 2026-12-01 to 2026-12-03; organizer exhibitor update 2026-05-20.
ask: Attend TRE 2026 as a visitor to meet run-specialty buyers; consider a booth for 2027 when product ships.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band for runners' recovery, consumer launch May 2027. We'd like to meet run specialty retailers at TRE. Is there an emerging-brand or first-time exhibitor option, or a way for a pre-launch brand to attend and meet buyers?
entry_route: Exhibit or attend via the organizer, Diversified Communications (TRE site); no official application URL surfaced in search.
opportunity: Meet independent run-specialty buyers (the specialty running store channel) in one place, ahead of the 2027 retail plan.
unknowns: Official exhibitor application page and price not found (a third-party agency lists a 9 sqm booth at USD 5,880; unverified). Whether pre-launch brands can exhibit or attend as non-retailers is unknown.

name: Crunch Fitness brand partnerships
why: Crunch's brand partnerships page offers brands co-branded social campaigns, giveaways and member offers via Crunch Deals; equipment and tech suppliers separately earn Approved Vendor Partner status (e.g. Interactive Strength's CLMBR in 2024 after a club pilot; Freemotion in March 2026).
why_now: Freemotion named approved global vendor, March 2026.
ask: Propose a Crunch Deals member offer plus a small single-club pilot for launch.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band with no required subscription, consumer launch May 2027. Your brand partnerships page mentions member offers and co-branded campaigns. Could we talk about a launch offer for Crunch members, and what a club-level pilot would involve?
entry_route: Brand partnerships page at crunch.com/brand-partnerships for marketing; approved-vendor track via corporate and the invite-only franchise convention.
opportunity: Member-offer marketing at launch; longer term, Approved Vendor Partner status via a club pilot (CLMBR precedent).
unknowns: Contact form/address not visible in results. Approved-vendor criteria not public. The brand page still cites 400+ locations vs 550+ in 2026 coverage.

name: YMCA National Preferred Vendor (via YMCA Shared Services Inc.)
org: YMCA of the USA / YMCA Shared Services Inc.
why: Y-USA names National Preferred Vendors after they apply through YMCA Shared Services Inc., which vets on quality, pricing, service and mission fit; local Ys use the list to choose vendors. Recent national partners include Daxko (2024 alliance) and Peerfit (2021).
warm_path: Akron Area YMCA (Summit, Medina, Portage counties)
ask: Ask YMCA Shared Services what the National Preferred Vendor application requires; in parallel, ask the Akron Area YMCA about a small member pilot.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band with no required subscription, launching May 2027. We'd like to understand how a wellness device company applies to become a YMCA National Preferred Vendor, and whether a small pilot with a local Y is a sensible first step.
entry_route: Application through YMCA Shared Services Inc. (Y-USA's purchasing arm), per the 2018 vendor announcement.
opportunity: Preferred-vendor status lets 2,000+ local Ys buy without separate vetting; start with an Akron-area pilot for a home-town proof point.
unknowns: Current application URL, fees and timelines not found (2018 release is the only process description). Whether wearables are a vendor category the Y buys is unknown.

name: ProMedica Innovations - startup partner
why: ProMedica Innovations (Toledo, OH) takes submissions through an online form and innovations@promedica.org, and says it engages with entrepreneurs as a startup partner with capital, clinical and operational expertise and a resource network; ProMedica Ventures Innovation Fund III invests in digital health and medical device.
ask: Send a short note to ProMedica Innovations asking whether an employee-wellness or clinician-sleep pilot with a wellness band fits their startup-partner track.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band and a developer SDK, with DevKits going to a few design partners this year. Your page says ProMedica Innovations partners with entrepreneurs. Could we have a 15-minute call about whether a small Ohio wellness pilot fits what you look for?
entry_route: Online submission form on the ProMedica Innovations page or innovations@promedica.org (email published on the page).
opportunity: Northwest Ohio health-system pilot partner (e.g. staff wellness or shift-worker sleep study under general-wellness framing).
unknowns: The intake is built mainly for inventions/IP from ProMedica's community; fit for an outside company's pilot is unclear. Fund III's current activity unknown. The evidence page is on a staging-looking domain; confirm the live promedica.org URL.

name: PerkSpot merchant network
why: PerkSpot is a merchant-funded employee discount marketplace used by employers such as MaineHealth, Northwestern and San Bernardino County; its merchant page invites businesses to join and reach employees looking for deals, with performance-based economics.
ask: Apply to list a launch discount for employees across PerkSpot's employer clients.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're launching a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band in May 2027 with no required subscription. We'd like to offer an employee discount through PerkSpot at launch. Could you share what merchant onboarding involves and how offers are placed in front of employer programs?
opportunity: Employee-discount channel reaching many employers without selling to each HR team.
unknowns: Merchant pricing and commission not on the page (a school-district page cites $250/yr for local merchants; not national terms). Employers can suppress categories.

name: Perks at Work partner program (Next Jump)
why: Perks at Work's partner site invites brands to list offers for its employee base (stated 30M employees in 52 countries), with free sign-up for one US organisation, reporting on views and clicks, and paid CPC/affiliate upgrades for the full network.
ask: Sign up free and test one launch offer with a single US Perks at Work organisation.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're launching a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band in May 2027, no required subscription. We'd like to test an employee offer on Perks at Work at launch, starting with one organisation. Could you walk us through how the free tier works and what the paid network options cost?
entry_route: Free partner sign-up and weekly demo at partners.nextjump.com.
opportunity: Free, measurable test of employee-perk demand, then scale on CPC/affiliate terms.
unknowns: Network-wide pricing requires a commercial discussion; terms not public. Employee counts are the company's own figure.

name: Navy Exchange (NEX) - Doing Business With Us (RangeMe)
why: The NEX 'Doing Business With Us' page tells prospective suppliers for NEX stores and myNavyExchange.com to create a free company and product profile on RangeMe, which matches the product to a category buyer and notifies the vendor after review.
ask: Create a RangeMe product profile tagged for NEX once launch pricing and photos exist.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band for recovery and sleep, launching May 2027 with no required subscription. Sailors and military families are an audience we care about. We've started a RangeMe profile and would welcome guidance on what NEX buyers want to see from a new wearable brand.
entry_route: Free RangeMe profile per the NEX Doing Business page; exchanges' made-in-America page app.rangeme.com/exchangemadeinamerica (2021).
opportunity: Retail access to service members and families at NEX stores and online; aligns with Vybe's tactical/military audience work.
unknowns: Category buyer for wearables and any made-in-USA preference are unknown; review timelines not stated. The 2021 made-in-America RangeMe page may be outdated.

name: Marine Corps Exchange (MCX) supplier partnerships
why: MCX's partnerships page asks potential retail suppliers to create a free RangeMe profile and says traditional networking remains an option; MCX buys merchandise by negotiation under full and free competition, separate from MCCS non-resale contracting.
ask: Use the same RangeMe profile to flag MCX and ask for a buyer introduction.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band for recovery and sleep, launching May 2027. We'd like to be considered as a retail supplier to the Marine Corps Exchange and have a RangeMe profile in progress. Could you tell me which buyer reviews fitness wearables and what they look for first?
entry_route: Free RangeMe profile per MCX partnerships page, or traditional networking with MCX buyers.
opportunity: Retail access to Marines and families; pair with any MCCS fitness (Semper Fit) conversations.
unknowns: Wearables buyer, volumes and terms unknown. Overlaps with NEX/AAFES RangeMe route; treat as one RangeMe submission flagged to all exchanges.

name: Army & Air Force Exchange Service (AAFES) product sourcing via RangeMe
why: AAFES takes inbound product submissions through its RangeMe page and has run calls for American-made products across 20+ categories including sporting goods; it says it wants to give small-business owners brand visibility.
ask: Flag AAFES on the RangeMe profile and watch for the next sporting-goods or made-in-America call.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band for recovery and sleep, launching May 2027 with no required subscription. We'd like to be considered by Exchange buyers and are preparing our RangeMe profile. Is there a current sourcing call or buyer for fitness wearables we should aim the submission at?
geo: US / Army and Air Force installations
entry_route: AAFES RangeMe page (per trade press); periodic made-in-America sourcing calls.
opportunity: Retail access to Army and Air Force members and families (stores + ShopMyExchange).
unknowns: No official AAFES page surfaced in search (evidence is trade press); current open calls and dates unknown; whether Vybe's manufacturing would count as American-made is unknown.
